description:
FILED s465 (Fable, 2026-09-02) from the USER discussion of #1034: "I assume it is a need to annotate what variables are used for what in the IR, yes?  In case someone wants to compile to C/C++/etc.  Are there more obvious internal information that we should export?"  Answer: yes, and most of it the compiler ALREADY computes and throws away at emission.

WHAT IS VISIBLE TODAY ONLY BY SHAPE (probe scratchpad s465 vis.pl):
    (let (($sum 0))                     ; = VarAnnotator proved: unshared, raw numeric slot
    (let (($buf (%pcl-str-buffer ""))) ; = S1 verdict: append-only string
    (p-foreach-range-raw ($i 1 10) ...) ; = loop var never written, no dynamic $_ reader
    (p-raw-params ($a__excl__0 $b__excl__1) ...) ; = params never aliased; the rename suffix is provenance
    (pl-add $i 1)                       ; = the sub is wantarray-INSENSITIVE (the absence of p-scalar-ctx says so)
    (p-scalar-ctx (pl-greet "bob"))     ; = it is not
A reader who knows the runtime infers all of this; a second backend (C, JS -- docs/js-target-plan.md Part I / II.2 reverse-engineers exactly these classes from the shapes) must guess.  The IR review already asked for two of the pieces and they were never done: Â§4b.3 the rename manifest, Â§4b.2 (done: the header stamp).

WHAT TO EXPORT, ranked by what a second backend needs first:
  1. Variable class per binding: box | raw slot, and the raw FAMILY (num, str, str-buffer, container), plus closure-captured (heap vs stack for C).  Source: VarAnnotator verdicts (unboxable, raw-numeric B-regime, S1, foreach_ro, raw-closure-capture).
  2. Per-sub facts at the DEFINITION: return family (Parser2 sub_info `returns` / _sub_return_facts), wantarray-insensitive, writes through its arguments (writes_args), contains a string eval, which outer lexicals it captures, prototype.
  3. The rename manifest: $x__file__0 / $x__lex__N / $x__state__N / $a__excl__0 -> the source name + the reason (ir-spec Â§2b.3 documents the suffix FAMILIES; the per-file mapping is not emitted).
  4. Statement source mapping: perl file + line in a FIXED grammar (today: free-text `;` echo comments, non-semantic by ir-spec Â§1).
  5. Aggregate element families -- NOT inferred today; user-hint territory (#1034).

DESIGN POINTS (decide before coding):
  - ONE VOCABULARY for proven facts and asserted hints, with a flag (:proven | :declared).  #1034's hints are facts the compiler did not have to prove; a debug mode (PCL_CHECK_FACTS=1) can CHECK both -- a fact block saying raw-num on a slot that later holds a string is a compiler bug made visible.
  - WHERE: a `(declare ...)` inside every `let` is the CL-native spelling but changes every emitted form (the gate has many shape rows matching that text, and ir-spec Â§1 says declares are droppable advice).  RECOMMENDED: a no-op macro `p-facts` at the head of each file / each p-sub body, one entry per name -- disturbs nothing, zero runtime cost, one place to read.  Grammar goes in docs/ir-spec.md (new subsection under Â§1 or Â§2b) as NORMATIVE; a consumer may drop the block.
  - Emission-only: no runtime behaviour change; generation bump; corpus-diff will show EVERY file differing (by the added block only) -- the bar is that the diff is EXACTLY the block (strip-and-compare), emission-ab RCDIFF 0, gate green, sweep TOTAL +0 (the block is a no-op).
  - Cost bar: compile-time budget 50 % (the facts already exist; this is a printer).

RELATED: #75 (clear IR), #1034 (the user hints, part b), docs/generated-cl-ir-review.md Â§4b.3, docs/js-target-plan.md II.2, docs/ir-spec.md Â§1 + Â§2b.3.

=== DESIGN AMENDED 2026-09-03 (USER: "the generated Common Lisp could have macros for variable declarations that contain the type") ===
This SUPERSEDES the "WHERE: a no-op p-facts block" recommendation above for VARIABLES.  The class goes ON THE DECLARATION FORM, as in any typed language -- the consumer reads the type where the name is bound.

SHAPE (proposed):
    (p-let (($sum :num 0)
            ($buf :str-buffer "")
            ($obj :box (make-p-box nil))
            ($x__file__0 :num 0 :perl "$x" :why :captured-by-named-sub))   ; the rename manifest lives HERE too
      ...body...)
    (p-raw-params (($a__excl__0 :num) ($b__excl__1 :num)) ...)              ; parameters get the same per-name class
    (p-sub pl-add (&rest %_args) (:returns :num :wantarray-insensitive t :writes-args nil) ...)  ; the sub facts on the definition
  - `p-let` EXISTS in cl/pcl-runtime.lisp (line ~3304) as the legacy "every binding is a box" macro and is DEAD in v2 emission (closure.t emits 109 plain `let`, 0 p-let -- verify over the whole corpus before reclaiming; grep Pl/ for emitters).  Reclaim the name; the expansion is EXACTLY today's `let` (a :box entry expands to the make-p-box binding, a :num entry to the raw binding) so runtime cost is zero and the sweep/bench cannot move.
  - ONE macro with a keyword CLASS from a CLOSED set, not one macro per class: :box (general scalar box) | :num (raw numeric slot, the B-regime verdict) | :str (raw string) | :str-buffer (%pcl-str-buffer) | :array | :hash | (:int only when #1034 hints or a future integer verdict supply it).  An unknown class DIES at macroexpansion (rule 12).  Per-class macros (`p-let-num`) are the alternative; one macro keeps ir-spec Â§10's inventory small and a consumer's dispatch a table.
  - Extra keys on an entry are optional facts: :perl (the source name before renaming), :why (the rename reason -- the ir-spec Â§2b.3 family), :captured t (closure-captured: heap vs stack for a C backend), :proven | :declared (#1034 hints).  A SBCL `(declare (type fixnum ...))` is NOT emitted from a verdict by default: the runtime runs (speed 3) and a wrong type declaration is undefined behaviour there; PCL_CHECK_FACTS=1 expands the class into a checked `(check-type ...)` at the binding and at every root write (the compiler-bug detector).
  - Statement source lines: a fixed-grammar form is still a separate item (a `(p-line N)` marker or a comment grammar); decide in the same task.

COST, measured s465: ~17 Pl/t files / ~70 shape rows match the `(let ((` text (parser2-01.t 23, parser2-02.t 14, transpile-test-10.t 7, clform-01.t 5, ...) -- rewritten to the new spelling as a STRENGTHENING edit (s377 four-conjunct rule; they are shape rows, the value rows are untouched).  corpus-diff will show EVERY file differing; the bar is a normaliser (a tools/ script that macroexpands p-let back to let, or an emission mode PCL_IR_PLAIN=1 that prints the old spelling) proving the difference is EXACTLY the declaration syntax: emission-ab RCDIFF 0, sweep TOTAL +0, bench inside the control band, gate green after the shape-row edit.  Generation bump; the three artifacts regenerate.  ir-spec: a new normative subsection (Â§2.2 "Declarations carry their class") + the Â§10 inventory line; Â§1 "declares are droppable" stays true (the class is NOT a declare; a consumer that ignores the class still gets a correct program, it just loses the information).

ORDER: (1) reclaim p-let + the :box/:num/:str-buffer classes (the three verdicts that exist) -- the whole cost is the printer and the shape rows; (2) :perl/:why on renamed names (the manifest); (3) p-raw-params classes + the p-sub facts plist; (4) source lines.  #1034 (hints) then adds :declared entries through the same macro.

=== IMPLEMENTATION NOTE (Fable recon, 2026-09-03) ===
The `my` declaration is printed as a raw CLForm node `['let', ['list', ['list', cl_sym($name), INIT]], ...]` at ~15 SEPARATE sites in Pl/Parser2.pm (grep `'let'` around lines 7857, 8192, 8531-8587, 8765-8849, 9040, 9840, 9918-9927; INIT is `(make-p-box nil)`, the raw-slot initform, `_fresh_container(...)`, or a copy form).  That is the rule-11 shape: no single declaration printer exists, which is WHY the class is invisible.  So:
  STEP 0 (byte-identical, its own commit): ONE helper `_decl_binding($name, $class, $init, %facts)` that every site calls, still emitting today's `let` -- corpus-diff IDENTICAL over 111 + emission-ab SAME is the bar (no generation bump).
  STEP 1: flip the helper's output to `(p-let ((NAME CLASS INIT ...facts)) ...)`; the runtime's legacy `p-let` (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp ~3304, dead in v2 emission -- confirm with a corpus grep before reclaiming) becomes the class-dispatching macro; generation bump; the ~70 shape rows; the normaliser bar.
  The class per site is already known at the site (which INIT it chose = the verdict): make-p-box -> :box; raw initform -> :num / :str per the VarAnnotator family the site consulted; _fresh_container -> :array / :hash; the copy form -> :box with :from-copy.


=== STEPS 0 + 1 IMPLEMENTED (s466, Fable, 2026-09-03; worktree s466-1035, merge pending its legs) ===
STEP 0 (commit cc1dd14, byte-identical: corpus-diff IDENTICAL over 111 + shapes, emission-ab lib 22/22 SAME): ONE declaration printer in Pl/Parser2.pm -- `_decl_entry($name,$class,$init)` (closed class set, unknown DIES) + `_decl_fresh` (plain `my`, class by sigil via the shared `_sigil_of`) + `_slot_class($vi_entry)` (the same VarAnnotator keys `_wrap_freeze` reads: strbuf -> :str-buffer, coerce num/str -> :num/:str, plain unboxable -> :scalar) + `_decl_let(\@entries, @body)`; sixteen sites routed.
STEP 1: `_decl_let` prints `p-let`, `_decl_entry` prints `(NAME CLASS INIT)`; the runtime's dead legacy `p-let` is REPLACED by the class-dispatching macro (`%p-let-binding` in an eval-when; expansion == the old `let`, proven by macroexpand-1 EQUAL; unknown class errors at macroexpansion naming the set); generation v2-611; the three artifacts regenerated (`tools/rebuild-pack`; `./pl2cl --extension lib/mro.pm > cl/pcl-mro.lisp && tools/tag-license`, same for warnings); ir-spec section 2b.2a (normative); Pl/CLForm.pm keeps `NAME CLASS` on the head line of a multi-line entry (shape-keyed: an atom followed by a keyword atom); 58 Pl/t shape rows in 9 files rewritten to the new spelling, each STRENGTHENED with its class.
DESIGN ADDITIONS vs the task text: (a) the class set gained `:scalar` -- the plain `unboxable` verdict is a raw UNBOXED slot holding the scalar VALUE with no fixed family (neither :num nor :str; the B-regime coerce verdicts are the typed ones), and the closed set had no name for it; (b) `PCL_IR_PLAIN=1` in the ONE printer prints the pre-s466 `let` spelling -- a VERIFICATION switch (not in Pl/Passes.pm; changes no runtime behaviour) whose only use is the normaliser bar: `PCL_IR_PLAIN=1 tools/corpus-diff.pl <step-0-sha>` IDENTICAL over 111 + shapes proves the flip touched nothing but the syntax; `tools/emission-ab.pl --env PCL_IR_PLAIN=1` over lib: 22 DIFF (the syntax), RCDIFF 0.
NOT DONE (the task's order (2)-(4)): the FACTS keys (:perl/:why rename manifest, :captured), p-raw-params per-name classes, the p-sub facts plist, source-line markers, PCL_CHECK_FACTS.  Sub parameters are the next step.

=== STEPS 2-4 (s469bg, Opus agent, 2026-09-04) ===
STEP 2 -- THE RENAME MANIFEST, threaded from the mint site.  Six rename sites
(_rename_spanning_lexicals, _promote_captured, _state_rewrite_routes,
_rename_state_vars, _rename_exception_mys, _gate_seam_my_shadow) call ONE
registrar `Pl::Parser2::_reg_rename($old, $new, :WHY)` with a CLOSED reason set
(:spanning :captured :state-cell :exception-global :seam-shadow; an unknown
reason DIES).  `_decl_entry` reads the record back as `:perl "$x" :why :FAMILY`
on the p-let entry.  The manifest is a file-scoped hash reset at the head of
`parse()` (one source per Parser2 object, parse is not re-entrant).  NOT
derived from the suffix text -- a printer that parsed `__family__N` would be
the shape rule 11 forbids.
  A RENAME HAS THREE CARRIERS, and the first version of this step annotated
  only one of them.  A `my` binds a p-let entry; a signature parameter binds a
  p-raw-params entry; a PROMOTED lexical binds nothing -- it publishes a
  package CELL -- so `:captured` and `:spanning`, the two families this task
  named FIRST, reached emission as nothing but `$x__file__0`.  Caught by the
  s469bg merge review.  Fixed: ONE new printer `_decl_cell` appends the SAME
  `_decl_facts` tail and ALL EIGHT Parser2 `global_decl_form` calls route
  through it (routing every site rather than the ones judged able to see a
  rename is the point -- a name with no manifest entry emits what it emitted
  before, so no family can be missed by a judgement call); p-raw-params entries
  became `(NAME CLASS . FACTS)` through the same reader.  Exception-set names
  keep plain CL `defvar`, whose lambda list would read a facts tail as a
  docstring, so `_decl_cell` guards on the declarer (belt: a rename never stays
  in the partition).  Runtime: `p-defcell` takes the tail and `%p-param-name`
  accepts it, both checked by the shared `%p-check-facts` against the same
  closed key set, both ignoring it.

  A NAME CAN BE RENAMED TWICE, found by re-closing the arithmetic.
  perl-tests/aassign.t renames `$a` -> `$a__excl__6` (exception-set) ->
  `$a__excl__6__file__2` (captured by a named sub), and recording the second
  link alone made `:perl` name `"$a__excl__6"` -- a spelling nowhere in the
  perl program, which is worse than saying nothing.  `_reg_rename` FOLLOWS the
  chain: `:perl` is the source at its root, and `:why` lists every reason in
  the order they applied.  `:why` IS ONE KEYWORD FOR A SINGLE RENAME AND A LIST
  FOR A CHAIN -- self-describing shapes, so a consumer that wants one value
  takes the last.  The intermediate entry is MARKED superseded rather than
  deleted, so an audit can tell "nothing declares this" from "a hole".

  THE ARITHMETIC IS CLOSED BY MATCHING, NOT BY COUNTING.  A temporary
  manifest-dump instrument (added, measured, removed; the removal byte-verified
  against a pre-instrument snapshot) joined every registration to a printed
  pair over the 111-file corpus: 283 registrations, 282 annotated, 0
  unannotated -- :exception-global 130, :captured 87, :state-cell 43,
  :spanning 14, :seam-shadow 7, chained 1; 417 `:perl' tokens emitted (a name
  can be carried by BOTH a cell and an entry).  The ONE absent is state.t's
  `$spam__state__6`, VERIFIED: its `given (state $spam ...)` statement is a
  ruled refusal, so the declaration never reaches emission at all.  (The first
  version's "129 = the count" was an arithmetic over p-let entries only -- a
  count that closes over the wrong population closes over nothing.)
`:captured t` comes from Pl::VarAnnotator's `nested_sub` verdict, published as a
new %vi key.  Deliberately the CAPTURE, not the capture-plus-event veto:
under-reporting is the unsafe direction (a read-only capture still makes the
binding outlive its frame in a target without native closures).  The scan is
text-shaped, so the key over-reports; stated as such in ir-spec.

STEP 3 -- (a) every p-raw-params entry is (NAME CLASS) from the SAME
`_slot_class` the p-let sites read (one source for the class; the runtime's
`%p-param-name` validates against the same closed set and returns the name).
27 p-raw-params forms / 50 entries in the corpus, EVERY class :scalar -- a fact
about the ANALYSIS, not a placeholder: the B-regime freeze verdicts exclude
parameters by construction (a parameter's initial value is caller-bound, not a
wrappable write), so :num/:str cannot arise there today.
  (b) THE THREE p-sub PRINTERS BECAME ONE FIRST, byte-identically (commit
b8934af, its own bars: corpus-diff IDENTICAL 111 + 6 shapes, lib 22/22 SAME,
no generation bump).  Then p-sub gains a FACTS PLIST at a fixed position after
the lambda list -- ALWAYS printed, possibly () (155 of the corpus's 661 print
(), mostly `use constant`, lowered by a path that proves none of them).  Keys:
  :returns :num|:str        sub_info `returns` (#77); absent when unproven
  :wantarray-insensitive t  TRUE-ONLY -- the walk answers 0 on any doubt
  :writes-args t|nil        BOTH directions -- `_sub_writes_args` answers 1 on
                            any doubt, so nil is a real proof
  :string-eval t            TRUE-ONLY, from the ONE eval scan
  :captures (CELLS...)      the promoted cells, from the promotion itself
  :prototype "$$"           old-style text only; a signature is not a prototype
Two sources had to be made to answer PER SUB rather than per file: the eval
scan lost its `last` early-out (the first eval the walk met is not a per-sub
answer) and `_inside_named_sub` returns the NODE; `_captured_in_subs` gained an
optional collector that suppresses its first-hit early-out, so `_promote_captured`
can record WHICH subs it promoted for (keyed by PPI refaddr -- two same-named
subs in different packages cannot be confused).

RUNTIME: the declaration vocabulary is now ONE eval-when block placed AHEAD of
all three macros (it had sat beside p-let, 2600 lines BELOW p-sub and
p-raw-params): *p-let-classes*, *p-let-fact-keys*, *p-sub-fact-keys*,
%p-check-facts (ONE checker for both plists), %p-let-binding, %p-param-name.
Every set closed; every violation an error at macroexpansion.

BARS.  PCL_IR_PLAIN=1 extended to all three new spellings (its ONE reading is
now `Pl::CLForm::ir_plain`, asked by both emitters -- Pl/Parser.pm's two v1
p-sub emitters print the empty plist and suppress it under the switch).
`PCL_IR_PLAIN=1 tools/corpus-diff.pl 57969a2` = IDENTICAL across 111 files,
silent drops 5 unchanged.  Form counts identical on both trees (2214 p-let,
661 p-sub, 27 p-raw-params); emitted bytes +0.91%.  Compile time on
perl-tests/pack.t, INTERLEAVED 5 rounds: base median 2.76 s, new 2.79 s =
+1.1% (budget 50%).  Gate 199 files / 6793 rows, only the 13 pclxs xs rows; guard Pl/t/decl-facts-01.t, 35 rows, 3 s
wall -- one per family per CARRIER, the identity promotion that is correctly
NOT a rename, the chain, `:captured` presence AND absence, and twelve rows
proving an unknown class / key / stray atom DIES at macroexpansion.
Generation v2-680 (rebased above main's v2-670); the three artifacts
regenerated on the rebased tree.  No sweep-visible surface: the expansion is
identical, so nothing the sweep measures can move.  28 Pl/t shape rows in 10
files rewritten as STRENGTHENING edits (each now asserts the class / the
manifest / the plist the tree emits).

STEP 4 -- DECIDED and MEASURED; NOT IMPLEMENTED, and it needs its own step-0.
THE GRAMMAR IS A COMMENT: `;; @ FILE:LINE` before a statement's forms, NOT a
`(p-line N)` marker form.  Two reasons, both structural: a marker is a real
form the host compiler has to see and delete, and in TAIL position it would
change a block's value (every `progn`/`block`/`p-let` body ends in its value);
a comment cannot change what is evaluated, and the IR already has a normative
comment (the pipeline marker, ir-spec 9.2), so the precedent exists.
MEASURED:
  * 39,717 PPI statements over the 111-file perl-tests corpus.
  * one `;; @ perl-tests/pack.t:1234` line = 28 bytes -> 1,112,076 bytes over
    the corpus = +38.4% of emitted bytes.
  * CL READER cost, the only cost a comment adds at load: pack.lisp reads in
    1.4 ms; with one marker per statement-ish line 1.5 ms; with one marker per
    LINE (the absolute upper bound, +60% file size) 1.8 ms.  20 reads each,
    *read-suppress* t so nothing is evaluated.  Negligible beside the compile.
  * THE BLOCKER IS STRUCTURAL: a per-statement marker would have to reach 71
    return paths -- _lower_block 45, _lower_stmt 17, _lower_compound 8,
    _lower_scope 1.  There is no ONE statement printer, which is exactly the
    rule-11 shape that made step 0 necessary for declarations.  So step 4 is a
    commit series of its own: (4.0) route every statement emission through one
    printer, byte-identically; (4.1) flip that printer to prepend the marker,
    with PCL_IR_PLAIN suppressing it and the corpus diff being EXACTLY the
    marker lines.
ir-spec 1's "comments are non-semantic" line is reconciled either way: one
comment is normative today (the pipeline marker) and this grammar is RESERVED
as the second; a consumer may still drop every comment and read a correct
program.

NOT DONE (deliberately, and why): PCL_CHECK_FACTS=1 (the optional
compiler-bug detector -- a class expanding into a `check-type` at the binding).
It was the brief's "last, only if cheap" item and the session's time went to
step 4's measurement instead.  It is cheap NOW that the vocabulary block
exists: one more `defparameter` switch read inside `%p-let-binding`, mapping
each class to a type and wrapping INIT in `(check-type ...)`.  The one design
question it still owes an answer to is what `:box`/`:array`/`:hash` check
against (a p-box struct, a vector, a hash-table) and whether the raw families
check the SLOT or every WRITE to it -- the task text says "at the binding and
at every root write", and only the binding half is free.

ZERO-RUNTIME-COST: `tools/bench-emission-ab.pl` CANNOT time this change, and
the reason is itself a finding.  It times two emissions against ONE core, and
step 3 changed p-sub's LAMBDA LIST, so the base tree's plist-less emission does
not load on this tree's runtime -- the tool answers "OUTPUTS DIFFER -- not
timed" with an empty B side.  The dispositive evidence is MACROEXPANSION: a
p-let entry with facts, a classed p-raw-params entry and a p-sub with a plist
expand to exactly the forms their bare twins do (macroexpand-1 EQUAL, four rows
in Pl/t/decl-facts-01.t) -- the compiled S-expression is the same, so there is
nothing left to time.  Reported anyway, with its spread, a coarse per-TREE
interleaved wall A/B (each tree on its own core, K=5, `scratch/s469bg/ab-run.sh`
in the worktree): sub-call-heavy base median 1.50 s / new 1.55 s with the base
series alone spanning 1.39-1.66 (19%); loop base 0.49 / new 0.51 with the base
series spanning 0.47-0.51 (8%).  Both rows inside their own control spread on a
box shared with two other agents; the merge review re-measures.

PCL_IR_PLAIN=1 OUTPUT IS NOW FOR COMPARISON, NOT FOR RUNNING.  The facts plist
is a POSITIONAL slot, so the plist-less p-sub the switch prints would bind its
`facts` parameter to the first body form.  That is the price of an unambiguous
lambda list -- the alternative, a macro that SNIFFS whether the third form is a
plist, is exactly the ambiguity "print it always, possibly ()" was chosen to
avoid -- and it costs nothing, because the switch's only consumer is a byte-diff
against a tree that predates the step.  Stated in Pl/CLForm.pm's `ir_plain` and
in ir-spec 2b.2a.

GATE: 199 files / 6771 rows, only the 13 pclxs xs rows (xs-01 5/6, xs-02 4/4,
xs-03 4/4), which the USER has ruled out of scope.

RESIDUE FILED, not fixed: #1095 (tools/bench-emission-ab.pl cannot time a
change to a runtime macro's LAMBDA LIST -- it times two emissions against ONE
core, so the base emission does not load; it should DIAGNOSE that instead of
reporting "OUTPUTS DIFFER") and #1096 (the package-QUALIFIED twin declaration
of a spanning cell carries no manifest -- the same cell IS annotated at its
primary declaration in the same emitted file, so it is polish, and the right
fix is at the spanning pass, not a string rule at the printer).
subject: EXPORT THE COMPILER'S OWN FACTS INTO THE IR (Target B, #75): the DECLARATION FORMS carry the class (USER 2026-09-03) -- reclaim `p-let` as `(p-let ((NAME CLASS INIT ...facts)) body)` with a closed class set (:box :num :str :str-buffer :array :hash), per-name classes on p-raw-params, a facts plist on p-sub, the rename manifest as :perl/:why on the entry; expansion = today's let, zero runtime cost; ONE vocabulary shared with #1034's :declared hints
